newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Duma votes to ban foreign insurance.
newsitem.headline: Russia Duma votes to ban foreign insurance.

text.p: The State Duma lower house of parliament approved on Wednesday in a first reading amendments to the insurance law, banning insurance companies with foreign licences from insuring Russian individuals and companies.
The only exception is third-party insurance for car-owners going abroad.

The Duma also ruled that the minimum authorised capital of new insurance companies not involved in life insurance should be 25,000 minimum wages. For companies involved in life insurance, it should be 35,000 minimum wages and for companies involved in re-insurance 50,000 wages.
Companies registered before the law comes in force are to raise their capital to these levels by January 1, 1999.
At present, the minimum required authorised capital for Russian insurance companies is two million roubles.
To become law, a bill must be approved in a total of three readings, approved by the upper house Federation Council and signed by President Boris Yeltsin.
